correctness.summary: The random greedy output on a complete multipartite graph is exactly the part containing the first inspected vertex, giving the size-biased law and moment formula. The variance extremum is proved by conditioning on a largest part, an elementary bounded-range variance inequality, a reduction to one nonsingleton part, and an exact discrete-difference optimization. Boundary cases and the no-tie divisibility argument were checked; exhaustive finite verification supports the proof.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The recent triangle-free variance theorem arXiv:2609.14826 and the accessible random-greedy MIS literature were checked together with searches for complete multipartite, complete split, complete bipartite, variance, random sequential adsorption, and size-biased formulations. No equivalent or stronger sharp finite-order variance classification over connected complete multipartite graphs was found. The elementary exact law and bipartite special case are not claimed as novel.

value.summary: The result gives a sharp finite-n variance maximum for a natural dense graph family, uniquely identifies the extremal complete split graph for every n, yields the asymptotic constant 27/256, and makes the recent triangle-free star equality transparent in the complete-bipartite subfamily.

limitations: The extremal theorem is restricted to connected complete multipartite graphs of order n>=3.
It does not determine the variance maximum over all graphs, at fixed edge count, or at fixed chromatic number.
The full text of arXiv:2609.14826 was not inspected; its accessible abstract was inspected.
Older random-sequential-adsorption literature under different terminology and very recent parallel work remain residual originality risks.
Computational verification is supporting evidence and does not replace the proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
